olympic-1896.summary: The first modern Games, where Coubertin revived the ancient Olympics and 241 athletes from 14 countries competed.
facts: Winners received a silver medal and an olive branch instead of a gold medal.
Spyridon Louis, a former water carrier, won the first-ever marathon.

olympic-1900.summary: Games held as a sideshow to the World's Fair, stretching from May to October.
facts: Women competed for the first time, and tennis player Charlotte Cooper became the first female individual champion.
Some athletes competed without even knowing their event was part of the Olympics.

olympic-1904.summary: The first Games to leave Europe and be held in the Americas.
facts: Of the 648 athletes, more than 520 were from the host nation.
Gold, silver and bronze medals were awarded for the first time, just as they are today.

olympic-1908.summary: Games that took over after Rome withdrew because of a volcanic eruption, and first used today's marathon distance.
facts: A course starting at Windsor Castle and finishing in front of the royal box came out to 42.195 kilometers.
In 1921 this became the official marathon distance, and it's still used today.

olympic-1912.summary: Games that introduced electronic timing in track and field and saw Japan become the first Asian nation to compete.
facts: In 1913, the year after these Games, Coubertin designed the Olympic rings to represent five continents.
Jim Thorpe won both the pentathlon and the decathlon.

olympic-1920.summary: Games that resumed without inviting Germany, Austria and the other nations defeated in World War I.
facts: The Olympic flag flew for the first time, and doves were released as a symbol of peace for the first time.
Victor Boin of Belgium took the first Olympic athletes' oath.

olympic-1924.summary: The first Games to build an Olympic Village next to the venues to house the athletes.
facts: The film “Chariots of Fire” tells the story of the United Kingdom's track athletes at these Games.
The motto “Faster, Higher, Stronger” was used for the first time.

olympic-1928.summary: The first Games to light an Olympic flame atop a tower at the stadium.
facts: Coca-Cola became an official sponsor for the first time and has stayed one ever since.
The tradition of the team from Greece leading the parade of nations took hold.

olympic-1932.summary: Games where the Great Depression cut the number of athletes to less than half that of the previous Games.
facts: The medal ceremony, raising the winner's flag and playing the national anthem, took its modern form here.
Male athletes stayed in cottages in the Olympic Village, while the 126 female athletes stayed separately in a hotel.

olympic-1936.summary: The first Games with a torch relay and a television broadcast.
facts: Sohn Kee-chung won the marathon running under the flag of Japan.
Jesse Owens won the 100 meters, the 200 meters, the long jump and the relay.

olympic-1948.summary: Games held again after a 12-year gap following World War II.
facts: South Korea took part in the Summer Games for the first time under the Taegukgi, its national flag.
Weightlifter Kim Sung-jip won bronze, the first Olympic medal under the Korean flag.

olympic-1952.summary: Games where the Soviet Union competed for the first time and began battling the United States atop the medal table.
facts: Israel and the People's Republic of China also made their debuts.
Emil Zátopek of Czechoslovakia swept three long-distance events.

olympic-1956.summary: The first Games held in the Southern Hemisphere, opening in late November.
facts: Because of quarantine rules, the equestrian events alone were held five months early in Stockholm.
The tradition of athletes entering the closing ceremony together, mixed regardless of nation, began here.

olympic-1960.summary: Games that held events at ancient sites such as the Basilica of Maxentius and the Baths of Caracalla.
facts: Running barefoot, Abebe Bikila won the marathon to give Ethiopia its first gold medal.
Right after the Olympics, the first Paralympics were held in the same city.

olympic-1964.summary: The first Games held in Asia, with the Shinkansen bullet train starting service nine days before the opening.
facts: The Games were broadcast live across the ocean to the United States via the geostationary satellite Syncom 3.
Judo and volleyball, both hugely popular in Japan, became official sports for the first time.

olympic-1968.summary: Games held at high altitude, 2,240 meters above sea level.
facts: Bob Beamon's 8.90-meter long jump stood as the world record for 23 years.
After Fosbury won with his backward “flop,” the technique became the standard in the high jump.

olympic-1972.summary: Games halted for 34 hours by a hostage crisis in the Olympic Village.
facts: Swimmer Mark Spitz won seven gold medals.
Waldi the dachshund became the first official Olympic mascot.

olympic-1976.summary: Games where a 14-year-old gymnast earned the first perfect 10 in Olympic history.
facts: Yang Jung-mo won South Korea's first Olympic gold medal, in wrestling.
Because the scoreboard couldn't display 10.00, Comăneci's perfect score showed up as 1.00.

olympic-1980.summary: Games missing 66 countries because of a boycott led by the United States.
facts: Misha, the bear mascot, shed a tear in a card stunt at the closing ceremony.
South Korea, Japan and West Germany also stayed away in protest of the invasion of Afghanistan.

olympic-1984.summary: Games boycotted in return by the Soviet Union and 14 other Eastern Bloc countries.
facts: They're considered the first Olympics to turn a profit, thanks to corporate sponsorship.
Carl Lewis won four track and field events.

olympic-1988.summary: The first Games held in South Korea, bringing together a then-record 159 nations and territories.
facts: For the first time in 12 years, both sides of the East–West divide took part together.
At the opening ceremony, a boy rolled a hoop alone across the empty stadium field.

olympic-1992.summary: The first Summer Games held after the Dissolution of the Soviet Union and the Unification of Germany.
facts: Former Soviet republics competed together as a single Unified Team.
Hwang Young-cho won the marathon, taking gold 56 years after Sohn Kee-chung.

olympic-1996.summary: Games marking the 100th anniversary of the modern Olympics, where Muhammad Ali lit the cauldron.
facts: A bombing in a park killed two people, but the Games went on.
Beach volleyball and softball became official sports for the first time.

olympic-2000.summary: Games where the triathlon made its debut in the harbor in front of the Opera House.
facts: Athletes from North Korea and South Korea marched together at the opening ceremony.
Taekwondo became an official sport, and South Korea won three gold medals in it.

olympic-2004.summary: Games that returned, after 108 years, to the city that hosted the first modern Olympics.
facts: The shot put was held in the stadium at ancient Olympia.
The marathon started from the historic plain of Marathon.

olympic-2008.summary: The Games where China topped the gold medal count for the first time.
facts: Usain Bolt set world records in the 100 and 200 meters.
Michael Phelps won eight gold medals at a single Games.

olympic-2012.summary: Games that made their host the first city to stage the Olympics three times.
facts: It was the first Games where every participating nation sent at least one female athlete.
With the addition of women's boxing, it became the first Games where women competed in every sport.

olympic-2016.summary: The first Games held in South America, with the opening ceremony at the Maracanã Stadium.
facts: Ten athletes from South Sudan, Syria and elsewhere competed as the first Refugee Olympic Team.
Golf returned as an official sport after 112 years.

olympic-2020.summary: Games postponed by a year because of a pandemic and held in 2021.
facts: Because of COVID-19, most events were held without spectators.
Skateboarding and surfing became official sports for the first time.

olympic-2024.summary: Games that held the opening ceremony on a river instead of in a stadium.
facts: The South Korea women's archery team won its 10th straight team gold medal.
Breaking was held as an official sport for the first time.
